text:
Alice Nguyen: Heads-up — drift detector flagged a reconcile failure when promoting the network-policy Helm overlay from staging->prod. GPU workloads in prod are Pending. Error shows node taint mismatch and autoscaler skipped scheduling. Anyone oncall? :eyes:

infra-bot: Drift-detector alert: repo=infra/cluster-overlays branch=prod overlay/network-policy.yaml modified. Reconcile failed: argocd sync error. See logs: https://git.company/infra/ops/-/pipelines/9843

Ben Patel: Can you paste kubectl describe of one of the pending pods and `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath` output for taints? Also argocd app history?

Alice Nguyen: quick snippets from prod cluster (redacted):
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
node-01   Ready  64Gi  gpu: true  taints: gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule
node-02   Ready  64Gi  gpu: true  taints: gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule
node-old-1 Ready  64Gi  gpu: true  taints: <none>
```
```
$ kubectl describe pod gpu-trainer-7b6d -n ml
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3s  default-scheduler  0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taint {gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule} that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

Maya Li: That looks like a taint was added only to the newer nodepool. Did the Helm overlay apply a taint to the nodepool resource or did Terraform change nodepool taints?

Carla Gómez: Checked the GitOps PR — the prod overlay for nodepool values was updated last night. Helm diff shows a new values block in nodepool chart: 
```yaml
nodePools:
  - name: gpu-accelerated
    taints:
      - key: "gpu-reserved"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
```
This was intentionally added to isolate GPU nodes but the GPU workloads did not include the toleration. The staging overlay didn't have this because the staging values were left unchanged.

Ben Patel: Right — two options: 1) add tolerations to the GPU workload Helm chart so pods can run on tainted nodes, or 2) remove the taint from prod nodepool (hotfix) and do a coordinated rollout. Which is quicker?

Alice Nguyen: Also FYI OPA gate in infra-ci blocked a Terraform plan earlier today for nodepool changes (policy: nodepool must have subnet-tag=fleet-prod). The terraform diff showed both tags and taints changed; maybe someone merged the tag but not the tolerations for workloads. Terraform plan snippet: 
```
# azurerm_kubernetes_cluster_node_pool.gpu will be updated in-place
  ~ taint = ["gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule"]
  - taint = [] -> will be added
```

ops-automation-bot: Suggestion: create a short-lived reconciliation job to patch the GPU deployment with tolerations as a quick mitigation, then follow with proper Helm release to persist. Also consider adding a GitOps policy that runs helm-diff in CI to catch taint-only changes without matching tolerations.

Maya Li: Proposed rollback plan (minimal blast radius):
1) Add toleration to ml/gpu-trainer chart and open a PR (target: patch).
2) Merge PR and run `argocd app sync ml-prod --revision HEAD` to pick up the toleration immediately.
3) Monitor HPA/autoscaler and Pending pods.
4) After stable, update nodepool Terraform/helm values to include taint + update all workload charts to include tolerations, then promote to prod via normal flow.

Ben Patel: If someone can open the PR I'll prep an argocd emergency sync and watch autoscaler logs. I can also run `kubectl patch` as a short-term manual fix if needed.

Carla Gómez: I'll open the toleration PR against charts/ml with a minimal change: add tolerations block to Deployment spec. Pushing now.

Alice Nguyen: If PR takes >20m, I'll run a manual patch: `kubectl patch deploy gpu-trainer -n ml -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu-reserved","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'` and then roll pods.

argocd-bot: Sync started for app ml-prod (source: infra/charts/ml rev: feature/taint-toleration). Sync operation id: sync-7751

argocd-bot: Sync succeeded for app ml-prod in 01m22s. Resources: 4 updated, 0 failed.

Carla Gómez: PR merged and release pipeline kicked off. Helm chart updated to include toleration.

Alice Nguyen: Confirming pods are now scheduling: `kubectl get pods -n ml | grep Pending` returns empty. Autoscaler showing normal scale-up events.

infra-bot: Drift detector re-run passed: no outstanding taint drift between overlays and cluster state. Incident closed automatically.

Ben Patel: Nice — we should add a CI check: if nodepool taints are added in overlay PR then require corresponding toleration change in charts that select gpu nodes. Filing a GH issue for infra-ci policy: https://git.company/infra/issues/2216

Maya Li: Agreed. Also let's add a runbook step: when taints get added, update workloads first or schedule nodepool rollouts after workload updates. I'll add it to runbook.

Alice Nguyen: Thanks all. Quick and dirty but resolved. :thumbsup:

Carla Gómez: Thanks — learned a lot about the per-environment override pitfalls.

Ben Patel: :party-parrot:
